PROC SQL

Source: vignettes/articles/guide-sql.Rmd
guide-sql.Rmd
library(sasonr)

PROC SQL is parsed by sasonr’s own SQL parser. Joins and grouping run on DuckDB; SAS semantics are applied in R: missing values sort and compare as the smallest value, character comparisons ignore trailing blanks, summary statistics are merged back to detail rows (“remerging”) with the remerge NOTE, CALCULATED columns and INTO :macro-variable are supported.

Summaries, CALCULATED and CASE 

res <- sas_run("
data a;
  input g $ v;
  datalines;
A 1
B 2
A 3
;
run;
proc sql noprint;
  select distinct g into :glist separated by ',' from a;
  create table s as
    select g, sum(v) as tot, calculated tot * 2 as dbl,
           case when calculated tot > 3 then 'H' else 'L' end as cls
    from a group by g;
quit;
%put glist=&glist;
")
sas_log(res)
#> 1          
#> 2          data a;
#> 3            input g $ v;
#> 4            datalines;
#> 
#> NOTE: The data set WORK.A has 3 observations and 2 variables.
#> 8          ;
#> 9          run;
#> 10         proc sql noprint;
#> 11           select distinct g into :glist separated by ',' from a;
#> 12           create table s as
#> 13             select g, sum(v) as tot, calculated tot * 2 as dbl,
#> 14                    case when calculated tot > 3 then 'H' else 'L' end as cls
#> 15             from a group by g;
#> NOTE: Table WORK.S created, with 2 rows and 4 columns.
#> 16         quit;
#> 17         %put glist=&glist;
#> glist=A,B
res$work$s
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   g       tot   dbl cls  
#>   <chr> <dbl> <dbl> <chr>
#> 1 A         4     8 H    
#> 2 B         2     4 L

Remerging summary statistics 

res <- sas_run("
data a;
  input id $ grp $ x;
  datalines;
1 A 10
2 A 30
3 B 5
;
run;
proc sql;
  create table pct as
    select id, grp, x, x / sum(x) * 100 as pct
    from a group by grp;
quit;
")
grep("remerging", res$log, value = TRUE)
#> [1] "NOTE: The query requires remerging summary statistics back with the original data."
res$work$pct
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   id    grp       x   pct
#>   <chr> <chr> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 1     A        10    25
#> 2 2     A        30    75
#> 3 3     B         5   100
